jobs.prompt:
merge(cpp): final integration F1 of the native gateway: join the library line (stage 2b), packaging and guides onto the cross-line head

CONTEXT (you have no other context than this prompt and the repository)
You start from branch `agent-jobs/cppgw-integrate-x1-20261118-44302040764-1` of ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi (report `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-integrate-x1-20261118.md`): `cpp/gateway/` is a C++20 port of this repository's TypeScript gateway (`src/`, `serve.ts`) with a JavaScript-style runtime layer (`include/uos/rt`, `src/rt`, `src/runtime`) and vendored libraries under `cpp/gateway/third_party/`. On this state Linux ARM64 passes 445 release binaries and 5,054 cases. Every deployment target is 64-bit ARM.

OWNER POLICY (binding): generic functionality comes from mature open-source or standard libraries; exact parity with Bun's quirks and error wording is NOT required; less first-party code is preferred. What must hold: the gateway's functional behaviour (wire formats, status codes, stored data, authentication and validation decisions, accounting) and security never getting weaker.

READ FIRST: `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` (portable build-and-test driver: `bash cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh --config release --shard N/4`), `cpp/gateway/docs/BUILD.md`, `cpp/gateway/PORTING.md` (its coroutine rules are mandatory; its "Host safety" and "compile only through tools/unit.sh" rules apply to the authors' server, not to your disposable runner; where it demands exact Bun parity, the owner policy wins), your starting branch's report, and the stage 2b report named below.

GENERAL RULES
- The runner holds a model gateway token: never print it or write any credential to a file. Run tests with an empty `HOME`, a fresh `TMPDIR` and no provider variables. No real provider traffic: use local mocks only.
- Do not edit `.github/` (unless your task says so), the TypeScript, or `cpp/` outside `cpp/gateway/`. Do not delete or weaken tests.
- Model connections can drop: create your report file in the first minutes and commit small steps often (the tree must build at each commit). Leave no build output, binaries or downloads in the checkout.
- Report file: `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/<job id>.md`: what you did, exact commands, real counts and measurements, what is unfinished, defects found outside your paths (report, do not fix). End your final message with the same summary.

YOUR MACHINE: GitHub-hosted Linux ARM64 runner (Ubuntu 24.04, 4 CPUs, 16 GB, sudo, network). Its packages are too old for this tree: install Clang 21 or newer from apt.llvm.org (or GCC 14+), build Boost 1.92.0 `json` and `container` static libraries from the official source archive in a temp directory (the tree needs Boost >= 1.86), install OpenSSL 3, zlib, ICU, brotli, zstd development packages and build SQLite 3.54.0 as `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` describes. Bun 1.4.0 may be installed when you need to run the TypeScript.


OWNED PATHS
- anything under `cpp/gateway/` and `.github/workflows/cpp-gateway-*.yml` that the integration needs. Not the TypeScript. Vendored sources under `cpp/gateway/third_party/` stay byte-identical to the branch that brings them.

TASK
Your starting branch already contains LINE A (simdjson-only JSON, simdutf, central input limits, unified CI workflow, Beast outbound WebSocket, ICU, packaging, operator kit), LINE B stage 1 (standard-library helpers, llhttp server parsing) and the opt-in Landlock fallback. Merge the following reviewed branches, in this order, each with an ordinary `git merge` commit (fetch each from origin), building and testing after each:
1. `agent-jobs/cppgw-integrate-s2b-20261118-44298458094-1` (report `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-integrate-s2b-20261118.md`; 448 binaries, 5,086 cases on its own). It was built on LINE B stage 1, which you already contain, and adds: stage 1b runtime slimming (console, headers, multipart, environment, filesystem, containers, gzip), llhttp for outbound fetch and WebSocket response parsing, Ada for URL/IDNA/search parameters, QCBOR for passkey CBOR, OpenSSL for passkey ASN.1/X.509/CRL, Boost.Multiprecision BigInt, the stored-value (KV) reader fixes for sparse and cyclic values, the packaged conformance suite, and a cap on JSON and stored-graph nesting depth. This is the hard merge: LINE A changed many of the same files (JSON through simdjson only, WebSocket through Boost.Beast, the input-limits header, log records). Rules: there must be exactly ONE implementation of each thing afterwards; where both sides replaced hand-written code with a library, keep the library version with less first-party code; LINE A's deletion of the hand-written JSON parser stands (anything stage 2b wrote against the old parser API is ported to the simdjson-backed API); stage 2b's depth cap, strict CBOR/ASN.1 parsing and KV fixes stand; LINE A's Beast WebSocket client stands with stage 2b's llhttp handshake/response parsing only where Beast does not already do the job (prefer less first-party code). Combine vendor registrations (`CMakeLists.txt`, `cmake/vendors.json`, `tools/vendor_sources.py`, `tools/links.py` data, fuzz and packaging lists) so every library appears once.
2. `agent-jobs/cppgw-release-macos-20261118-44307885223-1` (release workflow `.github/workflows/cpp-gateway-release.yml`, `cpp/gateway/packaging/**`, `cpp/gateway/docs/RELEASES.md`; it sits on the Raspberry Pi packaging branch you already contain). Update its packaging file lists and licence set so the portable Linux package includes every library now linked (run `bash cpp/gateway/packaging/portable/build.sh` and its `verify.sh` once if Docker is available on your runner; if not, say so).
3. `agent-jobs/cppgw-docs-readme-20261118-44297533322-1` (`cpp/gateway/README.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`). Then correct those two documents for the merged state: test totals, the library list, and the confinement section (default Landlock requirement plus the opt-in reduced-confinement fallback `UOS_GATEWAY_ALLOW_REDUCED_CONFINEMENT=1`), and say that on macOS the packaged gateway currently answers only `--version` because serving requires Linux confinement.

KNOWN DEFECT TO FIX: on the hosted CI runner (`ubuntu-26.04-arm`, the unified workflow `.github/workflows/cpp-gateway-ci.yml`), `tests/rt/websocket_test.cpp` fails one case in both release and sanitizer builds, while it passes on Ubuntu 24.04 runners: line ~1211, case "close() validates like ws, leaving readyState CLOSING when it throws": expected log `[["close-ok",2]]`, actual `[["close-threw","TypeError","First argument must be a valid error code number",2],["second-close-ok",2]]`, and 0 frames sent where 1 is expected. Find the cause (suspect: a difference in the installed Boost or standard library version changing how the close code is validated or converted; reason from the code, and reproduce in an `ubuntu:26.04` arm64 container if Docker is available) and fix it in the production code or, only if the test's expectation is the quirk, in the test with the gateway-visible behaviour (a valid close code is accepted and one close frame is sent) still asserted. Also check the hosted run's "robustness (kv_jsc)" out-of-memory findings are gone now that the KV fixes are merged (run that fuzz target with the workflow's own command for at least 10 minutes).

Do not delete or weaken tests; where two lines changed the same test, keep the union of the cases. Record every conflict and its resolution, and every expectation you changed (before and after), in the report.

DONE WHEN
All three merges are in; all four release shards pass every binary and case on your Linux ARM64 runner (state totals; expect about 450 binaries and more than 5,090 cases); the sanitizer configuration passes at least the runtime (`tests/rt/**`), passkey, KV, HTTP and WebSocket tests; `python3 cpp/gateway/tools/links.py --check` passes; the packaged conformance suite (stage 2b report explains how to run it) still shows native equal to Bun on every case; the WebSocket defect is explained and fixed; the report gives first-party production line counts before and after, per-merge conflict tables and anything unfinished. Commit small steps often: this is a long job.
